{{Infobox person|gender={{ill|Male (gender)|qid=Q6581097}}|nationality={{ill|Japan|qid=Q17}}|father={{ill|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850}}|mother={{ill|Hibasu-hime|qid=Q8375821}}|relatives={{ill|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723}}; {{ill|Ojiwake no mikoto|qid=Q11620549}}; {{ill|Homutsuwake no Mikoto|qid=Q11631423}}; {{ill|Prince Ikatarashihiko|qid=Q11372186}}; {{ill|Prince Ikobayawake no Mikoto|qid=Q11492324}}; {{ill|Iwatsukiwake no Mikoto|qid=Q11587884}}; {{ill|Prince Tuburame|qid=Q11394830}}; {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732}}|native_name=五十瓊敷入彦命}}
[[File:Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|260px|right|{{center|Legendary Tomb (Udo no Haka) of Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto}}{{small|({{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}・{{ill|Sennan District, Osaka|en|Sennan District, Osaka|qid=Q1205635|lt=Sennan District}}・{{ill|Misaki, Osaka|en|Misaki, Osaka|qid=Q1358900|lt=Misaki Town}}の{{ill|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|de|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|ja|淡輪ニサンザイ古墳|zh|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun}}) }}]]
'''Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto''' (五十瓊敷入彦命{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}) was an ancient {{ill|Imperial Family of Japan|ja|皇族|zh|日本皇族|qid=Q11581068}} known from the {{ill|Kiki|en|Kiki|qid=Q294330|lt=Kiki}} texts.

In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', he is called “Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto”, “Inishiki no Mikoto”, or “Inishiki Ōji”, and in the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' as '''Inshiki Irihiko no Mikoto'''.

He was a son of the 11th {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}} and the elder full brother of the 12th {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}. He is famous in the legends concerning the sacred treasures of {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}} in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|en|Tenri, Nara|qid=Q502196|lt=Tenri}}.

== Genealogy ==
{{smaller|(Names follow ''Nihon Shoki'' first, with ''Kojiki'' names in parentheses)}}

According to both the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' and the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'', he was born to {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}} and the later Empress {{ill|Hibasu-hime|de|Hibasu-hime no Mikoto|ja|日葉酢媛命|zh|Hibasu-hime no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8375821}}.

Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto was the eldest, and the texts record four full siblings:
* Younger brother: {{ill|Otari-hiko no Mikoto|de|Otari-hiko no Mikoto|ja|大足彦尊|zh|Otari-hiko no Mikoto}} – the 12th '''{{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}'''.
* Younger sister: {{ill|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto|de|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto|ja|大中姫命|zh|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto}} (the ''Kojiki'' names the male {{ill|Ōnakatsu-hiko no Mikoto|de|Ōnakatsu-hiko no Mikoto|ja|大中津日子命|zh|Ōnakatsu-hiko no Mikoto}}).
* Younger sister: {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamato-hime no Mikoto}}.
* Younger brother: {{ill|Wakaki Niiri-hiko no Mikoto|de|Wakaki Niiri-hiko no Mikoto|ja|稚城瓊入彦命|zh|Wakaki Niiri-hiko no Mikoto}}.

== Records ==
In the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', the following deeds are recorded for Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}:
* Year 30, January 6 of Emperor Suinin’s reign:
** When asked what they desired, Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto chose bows and arrows, and Otari-hiko no Mikoto chose the throne. The emperor granted bows and arrows to Inishiki, and told Otari-hiko to succeed to the throne{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.
* Year 35, September:
** He was dispatched to {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}, where he excavated {{ill|Takaishi Pond|de|Takaishi Pond|ja|高石池|zh|Takaishi Pond}} in {{ill|Takaishi, Osaka|ar|تاكايشي (أوساكا)|ca|Takaishi|ce|Такаиси|ceb|Takaishi Shi|de|Takaishi|eo|Takaiŝi|es|Takaishi (Osaka)|et|Takaishi|fa|تاکایشی، اوساکا|fi|Takaishi|fr|Takaishi|gl|Takaishi|he|טקאישי|hy|Տակաիսի|it|Takaishi|ja|高石市|ko|다카이시시|mg|Takaishi|mzn|تاکایشی، اوساکا|nl|Takaishi|pl|Takaishi|pt|Takaishi (Osaka)|ro|Takaishi|ru|Такаиси|simple|Takaishi, Osaka|sv|Takaishi|tg|Такаишӣ|th|ทากาอิชิ|tl|Takaishi, Osaka|tr|Takaishi|tt|Такаиси|uk|Такаїші|ur|ٹاکائیشی، اوساکا|vi|Takaishi, Ōsaka|war|Takaishi, Osaka|zh|高石市|zh_classical|高石市|zh_min_nan|Takaisi-chhī|zh_yue|高石|qid=Q857218|lt=Takaishi}} and {{ill|Chinui Pond|de|Chinui Pond|ja|茅渟池|zh|Chinui Pond}} in {{ill|Izumisano|en|Izumisano|qid=Q852018|lt=Izumisano}}{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.
[[File:Isonokami-jingu, haiden-2.jpg|thumb|200px|right|{{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}} in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|en|Tenri, Nara|qid=Q502196|lt=Tenri}}]]
* Year 39, October:
** At the {{ill|Upper Uto River Shrine|de|Upper Uto River Shrine|ja|菟砥川上宮|zh|Upper Uto River Shrine}} in the {{ill|Uto River basin|de|Uto River basin|ja|菟砥川流域|zh|Uto River basin}} (in {{ill|Hannan|en|Hannan|qid=Q350174|lt=Hannan}}, {{ill|Sennan District, Osaka|en|Sennan District, Osaka|qid=Q1205635|lt=Sennan District}}), he forged 1,000 swords and dedicated them to {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}}. From then on, he oversaw the shrine’s treasures{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.
** An alternate account says he had 1,000 great swords forged, receiving ten crafts offices (品部): {{ill|Tatebe|de|Tatebe|ja|楯部|zh|Tatebe}}, {{ill|Worabe|de|Worabe|ja|倭文部|zh|Worabe}}, {{ill|Kamiyugebe|de|Kamiyugebe|ja|神弓削部|zh|Kamiyugebe}}, {{ill|Kamiyazukuri-be|de|Kamiyazukuri-be|ja|神矢作部|zh|Kamiyazukuri-be}}, {{ill|Ōanasobe|de|Ōanasobe|ja|大穴磯部|zh|Ōanasobe}}, {{ill|Tomashikibe|de|Tomashikibe|ja|泊橿部|zh|Tomashikibe}}, {{ill|Tamakurabe|de|Tamakurabe|ja|玉作部|zh|Tamakurabe}}, {{ill|Kamikōbe|de|Kamikōbe|ja|神刑部|zh|Kamikōbe}}, {{ill|Hiokibe|de|Hiokibe|ja|日置部|zh|Hiokibe}}, and {{ill|Ōtōhaibe|de|Ōtōhaibe|ja|大刀佩部|zh|Ōtōhaibe}}. Those swords were moved from {{ill|Oshisaka Village|de|Oshisaka Village|ja|忍坂邑|zh|Oshisaka Village}} to {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}}{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.
* Year 87, February 5:
** Due to old age, he entrusted oversight of the shrine’s treasures to his sister {{ill|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto|de|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto|ja|大中姫命|zh|Ōnakatsu-hime no Mikoto}}. She, citing her delicate health, passed them to {{ill|Mononobe no Tokone|de|Mononobe no Tokotsune|ja|物部十千根|zh|Mononobe no Tokotsune|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24885356}}, establishing the Mononobe clan’s stewardship{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.

In the ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' entry for Emperor Suinin, he is credited with creating {{ill|Chinui Pond|de|Chinui Pond|ja|茅渟池|zh|Chinui Pond}}, {{ill|Q11571742|de|Sayama Pond|ja|狭山池|zh|Sayama Pond|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11571742}} in {{ill|Ōsakasayama|en|Ōsakasayama|qid=Q385864|lt=Osakasayama}}, and a pond at {{ill|Kusaka|de|Kusaka|ja|日下|zh|Kusaka}}, and with forging 1,000 swords at {{ill|Tottori River Upper Shrine|de|Tottori River Upper Shrine|ja|鳥取河上宮|zh|Tottori River Upper Shrine}} for {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|en|Isonokami Shrine|qid=Q708859|lt=Isonokami Shrine}}. He also organized the Kawakami tribe there{{Sfn|五十瓊敷入彦命（古代氏族）|2010年}}.

== Tomb ==
[[File:Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun haisho-1.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Udo no Haka (宇度墓), the tomb of Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto at {{ill|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|de|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|ja|淡輪ニサンザイ古墳|zh|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun}}, {{ill|Misaki, Osaka|en|Misaki, Osaka|qid=Q1358900|lt=Misaki Town}}}}]]
The tomb, designated by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ar|وكالة رعاية القصر الإمبراطوري|ca|Agència de la Casa Imperial|de|Kaiserliches Hofamt|es|Agencia de la Casa Imperial|fa|دفتر خاندان امپراتوری|fr|Agence impériale|ha|Hukumar Kula da Gidajen Daular|he|סוכנות משק הבית הקיסרי|hr|Uprava japanskog carskog dvora|id|Badan Rumah Tangga Kekaisaran|it|Agenzia della Casa Imperiale|ja|宮内庁|ko|일본 궁내청|lt|Imperatoriškosios šeimos agentūra|min|Badan Rumah Tanggo Kakaisaran|ms|Agensi Rumah Tangga Imperial|nl|Japans hof|pl|Agencja Dworu Cesarskiego|pt|Agência da Casa Imperial|ru|Управление Императорского двора Японии|simple|Imperial Household Agency|th|สำนักพระราชวังหลวง (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|İmparatorluk Sarayı Ajansı|uk|Управління Імператорського двору Японії|vi|Cơ quan nội chính Hoàng gia Nhật Bản|zh|宫内厅|qid=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency}}, is the '''Udo no Haka''' (宇度墓, {{Coord|34|19|49.67|N|135|10|43.49|E|region:JP-27|name=Udo no Haka (Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto’s tomb)}}) in {{ill|Tannowa|de|Tannowa|ja|淡輪|zh|Tannowa|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11559834}}, {{ill|Misaki, Osaka|en|Misaki, Osaka|qid=Q1358900|lt=Misaki Town}}, {{ill|Sennan District, Osaka|en|Sennan District, Osaka|qid=Q1205635|lt=Sennan District}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} called {{ill|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|de|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun|ja|淡輪ニサンザイ古墳|zh|Tannowa Nisanzai Kofun}}, 200 m long.

Although not mentioned in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'' or ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'', the ''{{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}'' (927) lists “Udo no Haka” in {{ill|Izumi Province|en|Izumi Province|qid=Q1047117|lt=Izumi Province}}, {{ill|Hine district|de|Hine District|ja|日根郡|zh|Hine District|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11509546}}, with precincts of 3 chō east–west by 3 chō north–south, guarded by 3 households, classed as a remote tomb. An earlier 691 decree established three guard households at royal tombs of merit; scholars suggest this reflects parallel tomb-designations based on older records like the ''{{ill|Teiki|en|Teiki|qid=Q1107261|lt=Teiki}}'' and ''{{ill|Kyūji|en|Kyūji|qid=Q1107210|lt=Kyuji}}''. One theory holds that the tombs of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}}, {{ill|Itsuse no Mikoto|en|Itsuse no Mikoto|qid=Q10881970|lt=Hikoisosenu no Mikoto}}, Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto, and {{ill|Uji no Wakiiratsuko|de|Todo Chikarako|ja|菟道稚郎子|zh|Todo Chikarako|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11619989}} formed the four boundaries of {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}}<ref>{{Harvid|仁藤}}</ref>.

The tomb fell into ruin in the medieval period{{Sfn|宇度墓（国史）}}. In 1874, based on the ''{{ill|Senshūshi|de|Senshūshi|ja|泉州志|zh|Senshūshi}}'', it was located on Mt. Tamada, but in 1880 moved to the present site{{Sfn|宇度墓（国史）}}. The ''{{ill|Five Kinai Chronicles|ja|五畿内志|qid=Q11372555}}'' records it as the tomb of {{ill|Ki no Koyumi|de|Ki no Koyumi|ja|紀小弓|zh|Ki no Koyumi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605024}}{{Sfn|宇度墓（国史）}}.

== Legends ==
According to the shrine legend of {{ill|Inaba Shrine|eu|Inaba santutegia|fr|Inaba-jinja|ja|伊奈波神社|ko|이나바 신사|th|ศาลเจ้าอินาบะ|zh|伊奈波神社|qid=Q701414|lt=Inaba Shrine}} in {{ill|Gifu|en|Gifu|qid=Q45798|lt=Gifu City}}, Inishiki Irihiko no Mikoto pacified Ōshū by imperial order, but Murō no Kami {{ill|Toyomasa|de|Toyomasa|ja|豊益|zh|Toyomasa}}, envious of his success, slandered him as rebellious. He was then attacked as a traitor and killed there. His consort, {{ill|Nunoshihime no Mikoto|de|Nunoshi-hime no Mikoto|ja|渟熨斗姫命|zh|Nunoshi-hime no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q65272539}}, daughter of Emperor Keikō, left the capital to mourn him here until her death.
